issues.description: Specification is narrowed to ClassName without justification; the precondition for 'equivalent escaping' is unstated
issues.detail: The postcondition the author appears to claim is: two selectors that denote the same identifier should normalize to the same string. The implementation, however, only normalizes nodes for which parser.isClassName(node) holds. IDs, attribute values, pseudo-class arguments, and other identifiers in CSS also admit escape sequences and exhibit the same false-negative class of bug. The patch neither states why ClassName is sufficient nor proves that no other node type is reachable with an escaped value. This is UNREASONED: the frame condition (what may change) has been silently restricted with no argument.

issues.description: Correctness rests on an undocumented side effect of a third-party library; TESTED-NOT-PROVED
issues.detail: The mechanism `node.value = node.value` is correct only if postcss-selector-parser's ClassName setter is, and remains, idempotent and canonical across all inputs admitted by the CSS escape grammar. The author cites a single permalinked commit as evidence. That is not a proof; it is an appeal to a snapshot of someone else's code. The invariant required here -- canonical(unescape(x)) == canonical(unescape(canonical(unescape(x)))) for every legal escaped class name -- is neither stated nor tested across the relevant input space (surrogate pairs, whitespace-terminated hex escapes, escapes of ASCII letters, escapes at the start of an identifier, escapes of the digit that would otherwise be illegal as a first character). Two reject-cases do not establish this.

issues.description: The self-assignment is a smuggled side effect; the eslint-disable comment is the tell
issues.detail: `node.value = node.value` reads as a no-op to any reader who has not internalized the library's getter/setter contract. The author has had to silence a linter to permit it and annotate the type checker to permit the raws guard. Both are signals that the control flow is being expressed in a vocabulary the surrounding code does not share. A named helper such as `reencodeClassNameValue(node)` whose body performs the assignment, with the contract documented at the call site (precondition: node is a ClassName with a non-empty raws.value; postcondition: node.value is in the library's canonical escaped form), would make the reasoning local instead of folkloric.

issues.description: Performance guard conflates absence-of-raws with absence-of-need-to-normalize
issues.detail: The early return `if (!node.raws?.value) return;` assumes that a ClassName whose `raws.value` is empty is already canonical. This is a property of the parser, not of the program, and it is asserted with a comment rather than a test. If a future parser version populates `value` from an escaped source without setting `raws.value`, this guard silently reintroduces the original bug. A targeted test that constructs such a node (or, better, a fuzz over the escape grammar comparing pre- and post-normalization equality classes) would convert this from folklore to invariant.

issues.description: Test coverage exercises duplicate detection but not the normalization function's contract
issues.detail: Every new test goes through the rule. None goes through `normalizeSelector` directly. The unit under repair is the helper; its postcondition (equal denotations produce equal strings) should be tested at the helper's interface, over a representative set of escape forms, independent of the rule that consumes it. As written, a regression in `normalizeNodeEscaping` that happens not to affect `no-duplicate-selectors` -- or that affects some other consumer of `normalizeSelector` -- will not be caught here.

review.summary: The patch fixes the reported symptom and the two added reject cases pass, but the reasoning is thin. The author has not stated why ClassName is the only node type that needs renormalization, has not stated the invariant that the library's setter is canonical and idempotent over the CSS escape grammar, and has substituted two examples for a proof. The implementation hides its effect behind a self-assignment that required disabling a linter and the type checker -- a tell that the contract is folkloric rather than local. Verdict: TESTED-NOT-PROVED, accept conditionally on (a) a written justification for the ClassName-only scope, (b) direct unit tests of `normalizeNodeEscaping` over the escape grammar, and (c) a renamed helper that makes the side effect legible without lint suppression.
